title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional MONTH-end capping check effective at the open of 2027-04-30 (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2027-04-27 close), the family's pure monthly-vs-quarterly discriminator
source: EST: owner-published standing rule, DISPUTED BETWEEN TWO OWNER DOCUMENTS, both re-fetched and re-inflated independently by this lane on 2026-09-09. FOR the check: FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 content streams inflated in-session — byte count, stream count and version reproduce five sibling reads exactly, so the "a guide edition past v5.4" kill switch has not fired), whose section 4.8.6 gives all 20 Russell US Style rows frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45"; NEW THIS SESSION, the same table contains two contrasting rows reading "Quarterly" / "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" (FTSE Emerging ex China RIC 22.5/45 Capped Index and its Net variant), so the "Monthly" cell is a deliberate distinction the table can express both ways, not a default. AGAINST the check, and materially stronger than five sibling ledgers recorded: FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 streams) does not merely say "The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December)" in prose under a heading titled "Russell US Style quarter-end capping review" -- it also PUBLISHES AN OPERATIONAL CALENDAR whose rows read "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date: 26 March 2026 | 25 June 2026 | 25 September 2026 | 28 December 2026" and "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable): 31 March 2026 | 30 June 2026 | 30 September 2026 | 31 December 2026". Four dates a year, no month-end row, and every one of those four pairs reproduces under the same T-3 business-day walk this family uses to derive its 2027 dates. THE 2027 DATES ARE RULE-DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED: the last business day of April 2027 is Friday 2027-04-30 (no NYSE closure falls in April 2027 -- reproduced against src/domain/market-calendar.ts on all ten 2027 full closures), and a T-3 business-day walk gives the price date Tuesday 2027-04-27. The id names the EFFECTIVE date per the family convention. Stays estimate because the confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own methodology, because this lane may not self-confirm, and because the owner's two documents disagree about whether the check happens at all
notes: WRITTEN CANONICAL 2026-09-09 by the lane researching this id, after reading the single proposal that carried it (proposals/russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2027-04-30.from-russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2027-05-28.json). THE PROPOSER'S ARITHMETIC RATIONALE IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY AND THE ENTRY EARNS ITS PLACE: on 1,281 daily bars (2021-08-02 to 2026-09-08), modelling this check removes 16.53pp from the 2027-05-25 test's breach probability (36.64% -> 20.11%) and 11.93pp from the 2027-06-25 June quarter-end test (44.24% -> 32.31%), against the proposer's 16.45pp and 11.93pp -- so `FT-russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2027-05-28-3`, which asked whether an independent rebuild would put the marginal effect below 10pp, does NOT fire on this rebuild. THIS EVENT'S OWN NUMBER: path-simulated from the 2027-03-10 March review cut-off over 33 sessions with a conditional reset at session 11 (the 2027-03-25 quarter-end check), the check fires in 245/1,248 = 19.63% of paths (IWY) and 247/1,248 = 19.79% (IWF), against the proposer's 19.55% -- a 0.08pp gap. BUT THE EXISTENCE CASE GOT WORSE, NOT BETTER, AND THAT IS THIS SESSION'S HEADLINE: this instance is the family's PURE DISCRIMINATOR -- under the FAQ's reading it does not exist at all, whereas the quarter-end siblings (2027-03-31, 2027-06-30) exist under both readings -- and the FAQ side now carries a published operational calendar with exactly four capping dates a year plus a heading that names the mechanism "quarter-end capping", while the guide's own section 4.8.5 illustrative calendar (price date Friday the 25th, effective Wednesday the 30th, next day 1-Oct) is itself the September 2026 QUARTER-end instance, matching the FAQ's published 25 Sep -> 30 Sep pair. Keep the entry as a modelling input; hold the belief that the underlying check happens at a month-end at below even. ONE SENSITIVITY DOMINATES EVERYTHING THIS FAMILY HAS ARGUED ABOUT, stated here so no later lane re-derives it: every probability in this family assumes the March review resets the cohort to exactly 45%, and that assumption is worth more than the family's entire 4%-vs-8% dispute -- the same 33-session leg reads 13.22% from a 44% start, 22.84% from 45%, 38.22% from 46%, and 50.00% from today's actual IWY cohort weight of 46.81%. A one-point change in the reset level roughly doubles the answer. HOW IT WOULD BE CONFIRMED OR KILLED: FTSE Russell's 2027 Index Rebalance Market Calendar publishing a capping row with more than four dates confirms the monthly cadence from the owner's own schedule rather than from a table cell; the same calendar publishing four quarter-end dates again kills this entry and it should be WITHDRAWN rather than researched, as should a guide edition past v5.4 or an FAQ revision. The cheapest tape test is unchanged and belongs to other lanes: an index notice recording a Russell US Style recap effective 2026-10-30 or 2026-11-30. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the family's measured grounds: no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (0 hits in trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md, re-grepped 2026-09-09), and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on mega-cap beta. Estimate on a disputed rule with a conditional trigger; nothing here licenses an entry.
